title: What are you doing this weekend?
content_html:
1. Just finished writing a blog post about how I found a bug in TAOCP and Knuth named the theorem after me after fixing it. Spent the day counting page views, so I’m going to disconnect this weekend, go to the mountains and visit a festival.

    2. Sitting in a weird transitional space in life. Relationship is over, but neither of us has acknowledged as much as yet. Nobody did anything wrong, it's just kinda fallen apart. I'm not angry, would be so much easier if I was, just fed up and exhausted with the situation. Gonna be a mess, sorting out living arrangements and finances. So I'm just sitting with it for a bit.

      Idk, there's that, and also watching pretentious video essays on youtube I guess.

      1. I'm sorry to hear that, fellow human. I don't know you, but I care for you. I hope you find ways to care for yourself, too.

        1. FWIW I like your search engine

        2. 36 years ago my parents bought a small barren piece of land with the intent of growing a forest on it and building a cabin in that forest. They, and I as a small child helper, spent most weekends for a few years on that land, planting and caring for the trees, tending to the forest. 30 years ago the cabin got built. My father always talked about how one day the cabin would be surrounded by tall trees and how we would be able to cut down Yule trees from it. Sadly he passed before seeing that happen. I am now in that cabin, having taken up the mantle of tending to the trees, the paths and the cabin. And I now have helpers of my own.

          1. life goals tbh.

            If I may ask, got any good photos of the current state of the forest?

            1. Kind of OT, but I watched the love that remains yesterday and your comment reminded me of it somehow.

              Taking care of land passed down to us is beautiful, I agree.

            2. Going to Latvia and Lithuania on vacation, and meditating a lot on what it actually means to be sentient. Sentience is becoming a very interesting question to me as it seems like a continuous experience hsppening over time. Can an LLM which has discrete steps be sentient?

              1. I've never thought of sentience as it would relate to continuous vs. discrete experiences. That's very interesting.

                My (very Hofstadter-ey) take has always been that sentience requires some form of self reference or modification. I believe an LLM cannot be sentient because our current architectures are all feed-forward.

                That said I think an LLM can appear sentient, because as we scale the number of parameters its lower level of thought can approximate a higher level of thought. To me this feels like regular grammars vs. context free grammars. No DFA can match an infinite number of nested parentheses. But you could construct a sufficiently large DFA that it could match every string of nested parentheses a human could possibly type. That doesn't mean it's context free! Just a DFA that appears to be context free.

                1. I'm not really sure what constitutes sentience. Surely you are correct that self modification is part of it,but the fact that I experience the world in the present tense and not as a slide show feels like continuousness.

                2. A friend recently phrased one theory as something along the lines of "our brain does a lot of trying to predict what the world around us will do, and in groups of social monkeys it grows the ability to try to predict what other monkeys will do. Then sentience happens when it applies this predictive ability to itself."

                  No idea how accurate that is for real, but it sure made me stop and think a bit.

                  1. That still doesn't explain why we actually feel like we experience this process.

                    1. Like LLMs are deffinitely self aware but that does not mean that they feel anything, necessarilly. I don't know and it cannot be known. Just as no one can know how another sees a collor in their mind's eye.

                  2. Currently on the ferry to Isle of Man for a long weekend with a friend in the Z4. Was supposed to be taking part in a road rally event, but that was cancelled. Already had ferry/hotels booked so we're going to explore anyway, just at a more relaxed pace. Second time I've been there, looking forward to visiting again.

                      1. Junction Jam! it's a game jam in the MidWest USA where participants build a game while on a train to and from the hub in Chicago! I haven't taken many trains so I'm looking forward to it. This will be my 3rd game jam.

                        1. Last weekend, after months of slowly grinding, I got YEdit to run as a 16 bit program under OS/2 and render a file...only to crash as soon as a key is pressed.

                          This weekend will be the most exciting part of making it truly work.

                          It's currently 150Kb so has to be mindful of the 16 bit segmented memory model for both code and data, which has been an interesting exploration. And factoring code so that each part can be built in 640Kb with a 127 character command line has been an interesting challenge too.

                          Ultimately I'll get this to run on DOS 4, which is now MIT licensed with a bundled compiler/linker, and desperately needs a bundled text editor.

                          1. Where do you keep the code for it these days?

                            I was just curious to have a look, but the README of the linked repo suggests that the GitHub repo won't be updated in the future.

                          2. Clenching my butthole over a job interview I had today.

                            Other than that, some woodworking. I have started reading again and I am running out of shelf space for books and decided to make new shelves from oak wood myself.

                            1. I'm going to make some homemade dairy-free yogurt. Basically I make homemade soy milk. Add 1 cup of cashews blend in my blender for about a minute or two. Add some agar agar which I've bloomed in water. Pour it into jars. Let it cool to 110 Fahrenheit. Then I run it 110 in my sous vide water bath for 12 hours. But before that I put in my Thermopolis bacteria. So is it like Greek yogurt more or less.

                              1. I'm going through the corrections my student made to his PhD thesis after the examiners' feedback. It's the culmination of four years of hard work on his part.

                                1. Congratulations to your student from someone with an accepted thesis but no defence, and hence no diploma, yet! (The Dutch system is a little strange in that the defence/viva is a ceremony more than it's an exam.) I hope the journey was interesting and enjoyable from both your end and that of the student.

                                2. Learning Haskell, probably.

                                  1. Have fun! There's a lot to learn and a lot to enjoy. What resources are you using?

                                  2. Going to go scatter my cousin's ashes, apparently.

                                    1. My condolences.

                                    2. I don't know. I've had a stressful few days at work while the boss was away and tomorrow's a national holiday so everything's gonna be closed. My partner's on vacation. I might just sit at home and watch a horror movie or two, build an orc army in Middle-Earth: Shadow of War, and work on whichever of my project catches my eye after I've recovered from the work-related stress.

                                      1. I'm a hobbyist gamedev and I make games for old 8-bit microcomputers. I'm very close to finish the level design of my next ZX Spectrum 48K game, so I'm hoping to put in a couple of hours this weekend.

                                        There's still a lot of work to do, say 4 to 6 weeks if I don't get distracted, but I'm very excited because I've been feeling a bit low for the last couple of years (I didn't release anything in 2025 breaking a 10 years strike), and this looks like it this could be a nice release.

                                        1. I'm hacking on my "better Markdown" Zd. I think after another round of simplifying the syntax, it's time to rebuild the incremental parser. Getting closer!

                                          1. Looks like I'm going to be changing teams at $WORK on Monday - in that, a Director is putting together a team whose stated remit is a very close superset of the work I've been doing for the last few months, and has been asking my manager about my availability to move. (Un?)fortunately, several other folks at the company have also been doing similar work too; which means that the first problem that this team will have to solve will be "whose idea wins? Who gets to be Tech Lead?".

                                            All of which is to say, this weekend I'll be - trying to decide whether I want to struggle and politic my way to a leadership position in that particular group, or to take a backseat contributor role.

                                            Outside of work - nothing in particular planned!

                                            1. "whose idea wins? Who gets to be Tech Lead?".

                                              It doesn't relate to computing, but how do you resolve this when you don't have a good working relationship with all the parties involved?

                                              I personally wave the flag of maintainability over all else. Whatever is easier to maintain should win, imo, for being the lowest cost (in all terms) long term. Other than trying to persuade which can be a loser's errand... how do you socialize this kind of thing?

                                              1. I'm very accustomed to that being the attitude that would prevail, from the majority of my experience being in BigTech. However, my current place is a startup, where profit and sparkle are valued much more highly. It's been an adjustment.

                                            2. Installing Void Linux on my macOS.

                                              1. I have been getting into learning binary exploitation lately, and since everyone is saying the 90s and 00s were the golden age of that, I have spun up a VM with Windows 98 and Windows 2000 to try to recreate some old vulnerabilities.

                                                1. Testing out Qwen 3.8-27B on my local rig

                                                  1. Playing a gig at a local food and beer festival! It’ll be our third and last time at this festival, as the organisers have decided to discontinue it.

                                                    Also listening to a lot of music, and sampling all the locally brewed dark beers I can find.

                                                      1. A lot

                                                        • Working on some updates to my website(s)
                                                        • Working on an archival/distribution application for 3D artists
                                                        • Working on a context engine for content creators
                                                        • Going to my local redbull open skateboarding event
                                                        • Making a point to not spend all weekend on the computer and invest in some sun and some art

      My (very Hofstadter-ey) take has always been that sentience requires some form of self reference or modification. I believe an LLM cannot be sentient because our current architectures are all feed-forward.

      That said I think an LLM can appear sentient, because as we scale the number of parameters its lower level of thought can approximate a higher level of thought. To me this feels like regular grammars vs. context free grammars. No DFA can match an infinite number of nested parentheses. But you could construct a sufficiently large DFA that it could match every string of nested parentheses a human could possibly type. That doesn't mean it's context free! Just a DFA that appears to be context free.

      1. I'm not really sure what constitutes sentience. Surely you are correct that self modification is part of it,but the fact that I experience the world in the present tense and not as a slide show feels like continuousness.

• Last weekend, after months of slowly grinding, I got YEdit to run as a 16 bit program under OS/2 and render a file...only to crash as soon as a key is pressed.

    This weekend will be the most exciting part of making it truly work.

    It's currently 150Kb so has to be mindful of the 16 bit segmented memory model for both code and data, which has been an interesting exploration. And factoring code so that each part can be built in 640Kb with a 127 character command line has been an interesting challenge too.

    Ultimately I'll get this to run on DOS 4, which is now MIT licensed with a bundled compiler/linker, and desperately needs a bundled text editor.

      I was just curious to have a look, but the README of the linked repo suggests that the GitHub repo won't be updated in the future.

content_html_zh:
1. 刚刚写完一篇关于我如何在 TAOCP 中发现错误的博客文章，Knuth 在修复该错误后以我的名字命名了该定理。 我花了一天时间计算页面浏览量，所以这个周末我要断开连接，去山上参观一个节日。
  2. 坐在生活中一个奇怪的过渡空间。 关系结束了，但我们都还没有承认。 没有人做错什么，只是有点崩溃了。 我没有生气，如果我生气的话会容易得多，只是厌倦了这种情况，筋疲力尽。 会变得一团糟，整理生活安排和财务。 所以我只是坐在那里一会儿。 我不知道，就是这样，我猜还在 YouTube 上观看自命不凡的视频文章。 听到这个消息我很遗憾，人类同胞。 我不认识你，但我关心你。 我希望你也能找到照顾自己的方法。 FWIW我喜欢你的搜索引擎
  3. 36年前，我的父母买了一小块贫瘠的土地，打算在上面种植一片森林，并在森林里建造一间小屋。 他们和我作为一个小帮手，几年来的大部分周末都在那片土地上度过，种植和照料树木，照料森林。 30年前，小屋建成了。 我父亲总是谈论有一天小屋将被高大的树木包围，以及我们如何能够砍掉小屋里的圣诞树。 遗憾的是，他在看到这种情况发生之前就去世了。 我现在就在那个小屋里，承担起照料树木、小路和小屋的职责。 现在我有了自己的帮手。 人生目标说实话。 请问，有关于森林现状的好照片吗？ 有点过时，但我看到了昨天留下的爱，你的评论不知何故让我想起了它。 我同意，照顾好留给我们的土地是美好的。
  4. 去拉脱维亚和立陶宛度假，并深入思考有感知力的真正含义。 对我来说，感知正在成为一个非常有趣的问题，因为它似乎是随着时间的推移而发生的连续体验。 具有离散步骤的法学硕士可以有感知吗？ 我从来没有考虑过感知，因为它与连续和离散的经历有关。 这很有趣。 我（非常霍夫施塔特式）一直认为，感知需要某种形式的自我参照或修改。 我相信法学硕士不可能有感知能力，因为我们当前的架构都是前馈的。 也就是说，我认为法学硕士可以显得有感知力，因为当我们缩放参数数量时，其较低水平的思想可以近似较高水平的思想。 对我来说，这感觉就像常规语法与上下文无关语法。 任何 DFA 都无法匹配无限数量的嵌套括号。 但是您可以构造一个足够大的 DFA，使其可以匹配人类可能输入的每一串嵌套括号。 这并不意味着它是上下文无关的！ 只是一个看起来与上下文无关的 DFA。 我不太确定什么是感知力。 当然，你是对的，自我修改是其中的一部分，但事实上，我以现在时而不是幻灯片的方式体验世界，感觉像是连续性的。 一位朋友最近提出了一种理论，大意是“我们的大脑做了很多尝试来预测我们周围的世界会做什么，而在社交猴子群体中，它增强了尝试预测其他猴子会做什么的能力。 当它将这种预测能力应用到自身时，感知就会产生。” 不知道这到底有多准确，但这确实让我停下来思考了一下。 但这仍然无法解释为什么我们实际上感觉自己正在经历这个过程。 就像法学硕士一样，他们肯定有自我意识，但这并不意味着他们必然有任何感觉。 我不知道，也不可能知道。 就像没有人能知道另一个人如何在他们的脑海中看到一种颜色一样。
  5. 目前正在乘渡轮前往马恩岛，与一位朋友乘坐 Z4 度过一个长周末。 原本应该参加公路拉力赛，但被取消了。 已经预订了渡轮/酒店，所以我们无论如何都要探索，只是以更轻松的节奏。 第二次来了，期待再次光临。
    1. 路口堵塞！ 这是美国中西部的游戏盛会，参与者在往返芝加哥中心的火车上制作游戏！ 我没有坐过很多次火车，所以我很期待。 这将是我的第三场比赛。
